title: The future of money: What does tokenised finance mean for FX markets, liquidity and financial stability?
snippet: ‘Distributed Ledger Technology and tokenisation could fundamentally change financial markets, including FX markets’, said Bas ter Weel today at TradeTech FX in Amsterdam. He talked about ways to keep a tokenised financial system safe and stable, and how central banks are contributing to that.

title: Uncertainty dampens the impact of monetary policy
snippet: In times of economic uncertainty, the impact of monetary policy on the economy may be weaker. Moreover, a new DNB Analysis shows that not all forms of uncertainty have the same effect. Financial and geopolitical uncertainty, in particular, appear to be dampening the impact of an interest rate rise.

title: Trust in financial sector increases
snippet: Trust in the financial sector among Dutch households increased over the past year. This has emerged from a survey of almost 2,100 households conducted by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB). The share of respondents who have trust in financial institutions rose from 52% in 2025 to 57% in 2026.

title: Fine imposed on GMG Europe B.V. for repeated capital shortfalls
snippet: On 22 June 2026, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €59,770 on investment firm GMG Europe B.V. (GMG) for repeatedly failing to maintain sufficient own funds.

title: DNB improves tradability of gold reserves
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) has improved the tradability of its gold reserves by transferring part of the gold holdings from New York and Ottawa to London. This ensures that DNB is better prepared for severe crises.

title: Rising energy prices: what does this mean for prices and wages?
snippet: Energy prices have been rising since February, will this lead to higher inflation and wages? The 2022 energy crisis has shown that energy shocks usually do not have an immediate impact on other parts of the economy.

title: Fine for trust office International Trust Services B.V. for failing to commission an audit
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed a fine of €29,700 on trust International Trust Services B.V. (ITS) on 24 November 2025. The fine was imposed because ITS failed to commission an audit in 2022 concerning the period from January to December 2021.

title: From Magnum to SpaceX: households are investing in new names on the stock market
snippet: Dutch households have recently started to invest in several high-profile IPOs, including the spaceflight company SpaceX, the industrial and defence conglomerate CSG, and the ice-cream manufacturer Magnum. Overall, households enjoyed an exceptionally good second quarter.

title: Takeaway and food delivery services are having an increasingly significant impact on inflation
snippet: Takeaway and food delivery services are playing an increasingly important role in the Dutch economy. This is evident not only in everyday life, but also in inflation figures. The share of these services in the household consumption basket and their contribution to inflation have both increased.

title: Steven Maijoor to become Chair of the Trustees of the IFRS Foundation and to leave DNB
snippet: Steven Maijoor will step down as member of the Executive Board and Chair of Supervision of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) with effect from 1 March 2027.

title: The everyday work of inclusion
snippet: ‘Inclusion does not start or end at the top. It starts and ends with every single member of your organisation, in everyday moments’, said Olaf Sleijpen on 7 August 2026 at Workplace Pride in Amsterdam.

title: Pension transition and pension fund funding ratios – 2026Q2
snippet: The transition to the new pension in the Netherlands system is ongoing, with a growing number of pension funds having now made the conversion. In the second quarter of 2026, Dutch pension funds that had not yet converted saw their funding ratios improve relative to the previous quarter.

title: Fine for CCV Group B.V. for lack of SIRA
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) discloses its decision of 9 July 2020 to impose an administrative fine on CCV Group B.V. (CCV). DNB also discloses its decisions on CCV’s objection of 13 April 2022 and CCV’s subsequent appeal and higher appeal.

title: Dutch insurers and pension funds are investing more and more in private assets.
snippet: In recent years, Dutch insurers and pension funds have been investing more in private assets, such as private equity and private credit. By 2025, they had a combined total of €276 billion worth of these investments on their books. While the rapid growth of private markets presents opportunities...

title: Administrative fine imposed on CCV for inadequate customer due diligence
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €2.65 million on payment institution CCV Netherlands B.V. (CCV). We have imposed the fine because CCV failed to adequately and continuously monitor transactions.

title: Higher inflation is mainly driven by energy and transport costs.
snippet: Rising fuel prices and travel expenses are hard to miss. When households see these prices increase, it can seem as though inflation is affecting everything. In reality, price increases are not spread evenly across the economy.

title: Dutch supervisory authorities urge faster action on digital autonomy
snippet: Businesses procuring IT services should join forces more often, as this is key to strengthening their digital autonomy. Public authorities and businesses should make digital autonomy a core consideration in their procurement decisions, helping to drive the development of European digital services.

title: Fine for ABN AMRO Bank N.V. for inadequate customer due diligence for high-risk customers
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €8.5 million on ABN AMRO Bank N.V. (ABN AMRO) on 6 July 2026 due to serious shortcomings in its anti-money laundering controls in the period from September 2023 through September 2024.

title: Cash acceptance in the Netherlands remains stable
snippet: This is evident from the annual survey commissioned by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) on the acceptance of cash. Research agency Locatus visited more than 5,000 retailers and 1,000 market stalls across the Netherlands in 2025 to take stock of the payment options they offer.

title: DNB ATMs improve access to cash on Saba and Sint Eustatius
snippet: The first ATMs provided by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) opened on Saba and Sint Eustatius this week, making it easier for residents, business owners and visitors to withdraw cash.

title: Four questions about DNB’s new payment fraud figures
snippet: Starting now, DNB will publish figures every six months on the number of fraudulent transactions at banks and payment institutions. You can read here exactly what we mean by fraudulent transactions, and how these figures can be of use to you.

title: More fraud in payments in 2025
snippet: The number of fraudulent transactions involving bank transfers, card payments and cash withdrawals in the Dutch payments system rose by 30% in 2025 to approximately 658,000. As is evident from figures published by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) for the first time today.

title: Inflation: how households experience price increases
snippet: Inflation affects everyone. But how do different households experience these higher prices in their daily lives? A survey of nearly 3,000 households shows that many people are worried about their finances and their future.

title: Does monetary policy increase inequality?
snippet: There has been much debate in recent years over whether the European Central Bank’s monetary policy exacerbates inequality. Low interest rates and asset purchase programmes are thought to benefit richer households in particular, and others to a lesser extent.

title: Is it just a phase? The monetary policy response to supply shocks
snippet: ‘Incoming information suggests that the recent energy shock may prove more persistent than previously expected and that its effects are increasingly feeding through to broader inflation’, said Bas ter Weel at a monetary onference organized by the OeNB and SUERF, in Vienna today.

title: Lessons from 1763: the central bank as lender of last resort
snippet: ‘Banks may sometimes have the impression that using central bank operations in normal situations may trigger questions from their supervisor. This is absolutely not the case, and I think it is important to correct this misperception to avoid stigma in the market.’, said Steven Maijoor

title: Opening statement Steven Maijoor at the round table on the Market Integration & Supervision Package in the House of Representatives
snippet: The Netherlands stands to gain from a better functioning European capital market. That is true for the Savings and Investment Union more broadly, and it is also true for the Market Integration & Supervision Package”, said Steven Maijoor

title: Geopolitics, Trade Uncertainty and Inflation: Chimera or Reality?
snippet: ‘Monetary policy faces a demanding task: to distinguish between inflation that will persist and shocks that will pass,’ said Olaf Sleijpen at the European Economics and Financial Centre in London on 17 June 2026.

title: Racing the clock: Europe’s Journey to a Savings and Investment Union
snippet: ‘If you don’t want to lose a race, perhaps you should start acting like you are in one’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the Centre for European Reform, in London. He stress the urgency of making progress with capital market reform in Europe, and the need for renewed cooperation between the UK and the EU.

title: What if energy prices remain high for longer and uncertainty lingers?
snippet: Inflation and economic growth are linked to energy price movements. That is why we added two scenarios to our Spring Projections: an adverse and a severe scenario. Rather than predicting what will happen, they show what might happen if oil and gas prices stay high for longer and/or rise further.

title: The five key figures on the Dutch economy
snippet: Higher energy prices, uncertainty, and cautious consumers and businesses are holding back growth. Our Spring Projections show that the impact on inflation remains moderate for the time being. Below, we highlight the key developments in five figures.

title: War in the Middle East is holding back economic growth and driving up inflation
snippet: Growth in the Dutch economy is expected to be significantly lower this year than in 2025. This is largely due to the war in the Middle East, which has also caused inflation to rise in recent months. This is evident from the Spring Projections, published today by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: Order subject to penalty imposed on Yoursafe B.V. for failing to submit the independent auditor’s report on the 2024 financial statements or the annual accounts for 2024 by the deadline
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an order subject to penalty on Yoursafe B.V. (Yoursafe) on 5 February 2026. The order subject to a penalty is a remedial measure imposed because Yoursafe failed to submit the independent auditor's report to DNB by the deadline.

title: What an ageing population means for banks
snippet: The population of the Netherlands is ageing rapidly. While the implications for pensions and healthcare are well-recognised, ageing also affects the way individuals borrow, save and use banking services. What kind of impact will an ageing society have on banks?

title: The dollar is losing ground as a reserve currency, but remains dominant
snippet: The US dollar continues to play a major role in the global economy, but a shift is taking place. Central banks are holding relatively fewer dollar reserves than they did ten years ago. This is evident from recent figures from De Nederlandsche Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

title: Banks and payment institutions take action against payment fraud
snippet: Banks and payment institutions are paying close attention to various forms of payment fraud. This follows from an exploratory examination which DNB carried out in early 2026. All seven institutions we examined are taking various measures aimed at preventing fraud.

title: Fintech, supervision and smooth sailing
snippet: On 1 June 2026, Steven Maijoor delivered the welcome address at DNB’s Money20/20 pre-event in Amsterdam. In his speech, he reflected on fintech innovation, supervision and the shared responsibility to keep the financial system safe, trustworthy and future-proof.

title: Job switchers often move to a different sector
snippet: In more than half of all cases, Dutch workers who switch jobs also move to a completely different sector. These findings follow from the latest analysis by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB). Such labour mobility contributes not only to redistribution of the labour force among firms, but also across sector

title: Higher oil prices: putting the consequences into perspective
snippet: The price of oil has risen sharply as a result of the war in the Middle East. However, the economic impact in the Netherlands is less significant than in previous energy price shocks. Why is that?

title: Over-75s more and more likely to pay by debit card
snippet: People in the Netherlands are paying cash at points of sale (POS) somewhat less often than before. Just 17% of all payments are made in cash. People aged 75 and over are also paying by debit card more often and making less use of cash.

title: Heightened risk of cyber attacks and market corrections due to geopolitical unrest
snippet: Cyber and operational risks are currently among the biggest threats to financial stability, caused by a combination of the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) – which is increasing the scale, speed and complexity of cyber attacks – and geopolitical tensions.

title: From survival to partnership: how fintech needs the regulators, and the regulators need fintech
snippet: ‘Our door is always open. Our InnovationHub is open. We are open to dialogue and questions.’, said Steven Maijoor at the opening of the conference ‘Fintech meets the regulators’ at DNB today.

title: Households investing in the stock market benefited from buoyant oil shares in volatile first quarter
snippet: New figures from DNB show that Dutch households saw the value of their portfolio investments in oil companies rise sharply in the past quarter.

title: How supply chain disruptions are driving up inflation and how we can deal with this
snippet: Our economy depends heavily on global supply chains. Disruptions in these chains – for example due to geopolitical tensions – leave us vulnerable: prices of goods from abroad may rise, and inflation increase. Read the key findings from our Analysis below.

title: Disruptions to international supply chains are increasing the risk of inflation and call for European action
snippet: Disruptions in global supply chains are driving up inflation in the Netherlands and Europe. Central banks’ efforts to counteract inflation once it has affected the economy entail economic costs and fail to reverse the underlying supply chain disruption.

title: Different players, one team: why inclusion drives performance
snippet: ‘Inclusion is not a policy. It is a culture. And culture is built by all of us.’, said Olaf Sleijpen at a meeting of central banks as part of the International Day Against Homo/Bi/Inter/Transfobia (IDAHOBIT).

title: Olaf Sleijpen to become NGFS Chair on 1 July 2026
snippet: The Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) comprises more than 150 central banks and supervisory authorities that contribute on a voluntary basis to climate and nature-related risk management in the financial system.

title: Almost half of corporate lending goes to SMEs, interest rates slightly higher
snippet: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) account for almost half of all bank loans to businesses in the Netherlands, according to new figures being released by DNB for the first time today. However, SMEs often pay a slightly higher interest rate than other businesses.

title: Capital and labour still too often tied up in less productive companies
snippet: As the population ages, economic growth in the coming decades will have to come mainly from productivity gains. Healthy business dynamism and competition help boost such gains. A new DNB Analysis shows that there is still room for improvement on both counts.

title: Pension transition and pension fund funding ratios in first quarter
snippet: The transition to the new pension system is progressing, with a growing share of pension assets now having been transferred. In the first quarter of 2026, the funding ratio of pension funds still operating under the FTK declined, mainly due to negative developments in financial markets.

title: Number of financial holding companies owned by multinational corporations has almost halved
snippet: New figures from De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) show that the number of financial holding companies owned by multinational corporations in the conduit sector has almost halved over the past decade.

title: Garden of Choices: a triptych about our earning potential (speech held in Dutch)
snippet: On 22 April, Olaf Sleijpen spoke at the Jeroen Bosch Summit in Den Bosch. Drawing on Bosch’s Garden of Earthly Delights, he sketched a triptych of the earning potential in the Netherlands.

title: Marije Louisse appointed as the new Head of Legal Services
snippet: Marije Louisse will succeed Frits-Joost Beekhoven van den Boezem as General Counsel and Head of Legal Services at DNB on 1 May 2026.

title: Energy prices are rising: what does this mean for inflation and monetary policy?
snippet: The war in the Middle East is driving up oil and gas prices. This is reminiscent of 2022, when rising energy prices drove inflation sharply higher. But how similar is the current situation really, and what does that mean for inflation and monetary policy today?

title: Fine for AFS E-Venues B.V. for repeated liquidity shortfalls
snippet: On 8 April 2026, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €28,710 on investment firm AFS E-Venues B.V. (AFS E-Venues), as AFS E-Venues repeatedly failed to meet statutory liquidity requirements.

title: Resilient Payments: Cash, Card, Connected
snippet: ‘Resilience isn’t abstract: it’s practical, tangible – and sometimes it fits right in your pocket,’ said Bas ter Weel in his opening address at DNB’s Retail Payments Research Conference 2026 on ‘Future-proof payments: innovative, resilient and inclusive’, on 9 April 2026.

title: Securitisation market diversifies; residential mortgages lose their dominance
snippet: New figures from DNB show that the composition of the Dutch securitisation market has changed significantly in recent years. Whereas this market previously offered mainly securitised residential mortgages, it now offers a much broader mix of loans.

title: In a tight labour market, workers spend a lot of their time on non-core tasks, devoting a full day per week to meetings and administrative duties
snippet: Workers in the Netherlands say that, on average, they spend a fifth of their working hours on activities that are not part of their core tasks. Meetings and administrative duties take up the bulk of this time, particularly in education and the public sector.

title: Dutch pension funds invested more in Europe in 2025 and less in the United States
snippet: Pension funds in the Netherlands increased their investment holdings in Europe in 2025 and reduced them in the United States, as revealed by new DNB figures. They also disposed of a relatively large volume of equities to rebalance their asset allocation following the rise in share prices in years.

title: Marike Knoef appointed to DNB Supervisory Board from 1 April
snippet: Professor Marike Knoef will join the Supervisory Board of De Nederlandsche Bank from 1 April. Knoef has been appointed by Finance minister Eelco Heinen on behalf of the shareholder on the nomination of DNB’s Supervisory Board, for an initial four-year term.

title: The Netherlands has limited financial ties with the Middle East
snippet: According to new figures from De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), the total value of Dutch exports to the Middle East amounted to €47 billion in 2025, while imports totalled €21 billion. This means that the Netherlands’ trade with the region accounts for less than 5% of total Dutch imports and exports.

title: Uncertain times call for a strong Netherlands and a strong Europe
snippet: It is precisely in these uncertain times that we must strengthen the Dutch economy. And this requires a strong European Union that is more resilient and autonomous.

title: War in the Middle East: the impact on the Dutch economy
snippet: The war in the Middle East could cause inflation in the Netherlands to rise significantly, though less so than during the 2022 energy crisis. In a severe scenario, economic growth could slow down considerably. This is according to new calculations by De Nederlandsche Bank.

title: How do we keep the payment system secure and future-proof for everyone?
snippet: Payments should be secure and accessible for everyone, now and in the future. This requires extra effort in these times of geopolitical tensions and technological innovations. More choice is also essential, so that consumers, retailers and payment service providers have sufficient options for...

title: More choice essential for stronger payment systems
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) aims to broaden the range of options in the payments landscape. Consumers, retailers and payment service providers should have sufficient options available to execute payments.

title: Fine imposed on BondAuction Europe B.V. for repeated capital shortfall
snippet: On 26 February 2026, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €10,125 on the investment firm BondAuction Europe B.V. (BondAuction) for repeatedly failing to maintain sufficient own funds.

title: What do tariffs mean for the economy? Impact of import tariffs on prices, trade and growth
snippet: Import tariffs seem like a reasonable way for a country to protect its economy. But do they really work in practice? How do import tariffs affect the economy of the country that imposes them and the countries that are subject to them, and how should a central bank respond?

title: Relaxing lending standards leads to more debt and higher house prices
snippet: Being able to borrow more for a house sounds like a solution to the tight housing market. However, this would only mean higher house prices and more debt, especially among first-time buyers. Using a new monitor, we answer five questions on why adjusting lending standards is not a good idea.

title: Providing stability in an unstable world: the task of central banks
snippet: ‘Financial stability is often taken for granted. But if you work at a central bank, you know how much effort it takes to maintain it, especially when circumstances deteriorate’ said Olaf Sleijpen in his speech at the annual Congress of the Financial Study Association Groningen today.

title: Decline in counterfeit euro banknotes in the Netherlands continues
snippet: The number of counterfeit euro banknotes in the Netherlands is declining. A total of 17,900 counterfeit euro banknotes were withdrawn from circulation in the Netherlands in 2025, a 26% drop compared with 24,100 counterfeit notes in 2024. The €50 note was counterfeited most often.

title: Multinationals extend loans worth over €150 billion to Dutch companies
snippet: Large international firms lend substantial sums to their Dutch subsidiaries, DNB figures reveal. Their financial holdings – known as captive financial institutions (CFIs) – had extended over €154 billion in loans to Dutch businesses at the end of the third quarter of 2025.

title: Majority of consumers aware of advice on cash for emergencies
snippet: New research among more than 1,700 consumers shows that 71% are aware of the advice of the National Forum on the Payment System (NFPS) to hold €70 per adult and €30 per child in cash per household for emergencies. 58% of consumers actually keep this amount on hand.

title: DNB strengthens resilience to geopolitical risks
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) is taking additional measures to prepare for potential consequences of geopolitical tensions. In 2025, a resilience programme was launched to identify the main geopolitical risks and decide on the appropriate strategy going forward.

title: Standing with Ukraine, Strengthening Europe: Resilience, Growth and Stability
snippet: ‘Our role as a central bank may be modest, but we are fully committed to doing our part to support you‘, said Olaf Sleijpen in a panel meeting with students at the National Bank of Ukraine, in Kyiv last Thursday.

title: Households close eventful investment year on a positive note
snippet: Dutch households look back on a strong investment year despite considerable turbulence in the financial markets. Overall, the value of household portfolio investments rose by 7.8% in 2025, according to new figures from DNB. This brought total investments to €204.3 billion at year-end.

title: Economic resilience in an uncertain world
snippet: On 17 February 2026, Olaf Sleijpen talked about economic resilience in an uncertain world and what this means for Europe and the Netherlands. He was invited by the University of Amsterdam’s Economics and Business department at its annual EB NEXT! event.

title: Why the ECB has kept the interest rate unchanged at 2%
snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) kept the interest rate at 2% again in February. It has done so for five consecutive meetings, because inflation is stabilising around the 2% target, while the economy is growing steadily but still faces uncertainties.

title: Target additional defence expenditure for greatest strategic benefit
snippet: The Netherlands is set to spend more than €19 billion extra on defence on a structural basis. If we want to efficiently increase our military capacity with these additional billions, we need to look at where we have an edge over other European countries.

title: Repairing the vending machine: how the Savings and Investment Union is key to Europe’s future
snippet: ‘Europe’s competitiveness is on everybody’s mind. And well-functioning capital markets are essential for this’, said Olaf Sleijpen in his opening address for the Annual Symposium of the Radboud University Financial Law Centre.

title: Order subject to penalty on IDSG for failing to comply with demand for information
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank N.V. (DNB) has imposed an order subject to penalty on IDSG Group B.V. (IDSG). This is because IDSG failed to fully comply with DNB’s demand for information.

title: Europe’s Digital Autonomy: Between Fault Lines and Vault Lines
snippet: ‘Europe’s digital dependence runs like a fault line underneath our financial system. To protect this system from shocks, we need vault lines: strong structures and partnerships, built on shared values, that will reduce our digital dependence and strengthen the resilience of our financial sector.

title: Pension sector funding ratio improves in fourth quarter
snippet: In the fourth quarter of 2025, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios improve relative to the previous quarter, as the value of their liabilities decreased more than the value of their investments.

title: Caleen Financial Services B.V.’s licence withdrawn for failing to meet statutory obligations
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) decided on 29 January 2024 to withdraw the licence of Caleen Financial Services B.V. (CFS), a payment institution with offices in Tilburg, with effect from 5 April 2024.

title: Value of Dutch indirect crypto investments grows to over €1 billion
snippet: Crypto securities holdings by Dutch companies, institutions and households have skyrocketed in recent years, new figures from DNB show.

title: The Netherlands remains financially closely intertwined with other countries
snippet: The size of financial relations between the Netherlands and other countries has grown further this year, as revealed by new figures from De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: The Dutch economy in five figures: where do we stand?
snippet: The figures paint a remarkably positive picture: the Dutch economy is growing faster than expected. But where do we really stand, and what can the government do to address factors that are constraining further growth? Below, we discuss five figures from our Autumn Projections.

title: Dutch economy shows remarkably higher growth
snippet: Growth in the Dutch economy is significantly higher this year than expected in the spring. Whereas economic growth for 2025 was estimated at 1.1% last June, it is now projected to be 1.7%. This is evident from the Autumn Projections, published today by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: Bas ter Weel to join DNB Executive Board
snippet: Professor Bas ter Weel will join the Executive Board of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) on 1 March 2026, taking responsibility for the Monetary Affairs portfolio. Ter Weel is currently the General Director of SEO Amsterdam Economics.

title: Dutch financial institutions invest heavily in volatile tech stocks
snippet: Dutch pension funds, insurers, and investment funds now hold more than €200 billion in technology firm stocks, a significant portion of which is invested in major US tech giants. This is twice the amount recorded in 2020.

title: Dutch insurers acquire €7 billion in pension fund liabilities
snippet: In the past two years, Dutch life insurers have taken over €7 billion in pension liabilities through so-called buy-outs, according to new figures from De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB). For pension funds, a buy-out serves as an alternative to transitioning to the new pension system under the Wtp.

title: Corporate profits flowing to tax havens via the Netherlands continue to decline
snippet: New figures from De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) show that income from foreign direct investment and royalties channelled through the Netherlands to low-tax jurisdictions continued to fall in 2024.

title: Older bank customers have greener and more social attitude than younger generations
snippet: Dutch bank customers from the Silent Generation and the Baby Boom Generation assign even greater importance to a socially committed and sustainable bank than Millennial and Gen Z customers

title: Drop in carbon emissions from European bank loans
snippet: Euro area banks have been financing fewer and fewer greenhouse gas emissions through their loans to European firms in recent years, as revealed by new figures from De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) and the European Central Bank (ECB).

title: Awakening Europe’s Inner Animal: Building a Resilient and Innovative Economy
snippet: ‘If we manage to rise to the occasion, Europe could truly become an Innovation Union’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the Central Bank of Ireland Financial System Conference in Dublin today.

title: Instruction issued to trust office Pan-Invest B.V. in 2021 for shortcomings identified in its SIRA and customer due diligence
snippet: On 11 February 2021, the Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) issued an instruction to trust office Pan-Invest B.V. (Pan-Invest) for shortcomings found in its systematic integrity risk analysis (SIRA) and customer due diligence. As this decision has become irrevocable, it is now being disclosed.

title: Strengthening Europe in a Fragmented World: Integration as the Key to Stability
snippet: ‘Strong institutions and regulations ensure that new technologies and products are not a highway to the next crisis, but can be a true engine for sustainable growth’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the Euro Finance Week dinner at the Bundesbank in Frankfurt today.

title: Household investments break through the €200 billion mark due to rising stock prices
snippet: The third quarter of 2025 saw Dutch households’ portfolio investments surpass €200 billion for the first time, as revealed by the latest DNB figures. The growth can mainly be ascribed to rising stock prices.

title: DNB to make 10% budget cuts in coming years
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) strives to be an organisation that is agile, decisive and efficient in carrying out its tasks. This is necessary in a world rife with geopolitical tensions and uncertainty, accompanied by risks to financial stability.

title: Financial stability outlook remains concerning
snippet: Geopolitical tensions and global uncertainty about economic policy continue to amplify the likelihood of economic and financial shocks, posing significant risks to financial stability in the Netherlands. These developments are analysed in detail in the Financial Stability Report published today.

title: Trust in Dutch financial sector solid, despite growing concern about health of institutions
snippet: More than half of Dutch households have trust in the financial sector, which is similar to last year. At the same time, concerns about the financial health of banks, insurers and pension funds are growing. This has emerged from a survey of more than 2,400 households conducted by DNB.

title: Dutch households invest less than European average
snippet: Collectively, the Netherlands is among the largest investors in Europe. Few other countries invest a greater proportion of their national wealth in stocks and bonds. But if we zoom in on Dutch households, something stands out: they actually invest comparatively little.

title: With great power comes great responsibility: the case for policy coordination
snippet: ‘Since monetary and fiscal policy inevitably interact, our responsibility to coordinate them grows with every new challenge we face,’ said Olaf Sleijpen in his opening remarks at the Annual Research Conference of De Nederlandsche Bank, on 11 November 2025.

title: What is the Dutch share of EU debt?
snippet: In this article, we explain how much of this shared EU debt is attributable to the Netherlands, and why we will now include it in our assessment of Dutch public finances.

title: Why Dutch inflation is higher than euro area inflation
snippet: Inflation in the Netherlands has been higher than in the euro area as a whole for some time. In October, Dutch inflation was 0.9 percentage points higher than the euro area average. What is behind this trend and what can be done about it?

title: Pension sector funding ratio improves in third quarter
snippet: In the third quarter of 2025, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios improve relative to the previous quarter, as the value of their liabilities decreased, while the value of their investments went up.

title: Entangled in tech: financial institutions and their digital dependence
snippet: Banks, insurers, and pension funds increasingly rely on digital infrastructure to operate securely and efficiently.

title: New pension contract: implications for international interest rate markets
snippet: Dutch pension funds are on the eve of the transition to a new pension contract. This shift affects not only pension fund members, but is also being closely monitored by investors.

title: AFM and DNB warn of systemic risks in the financial sector from digital dependence
snippet: The Dutch financial sector faces increasing systemic risks stemming from its growing reliance on a limited number of non-European IT service providers. This is the key message of a joint report published today by the Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM) and De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: Speech Steven Maijoor - “Strong like a castle? Challenges for banking in a post-Covid world”
snippet: In his speech at the Cumberland Lodge Financial Service Summit today, Steven Maijoor urged banks to improve their risk management and not to release their provisions too soon in dealing with the Covid legacy. “Let’s not forget the unprecedented nature of what happened in the last 1.5 years.

title: DNB expects Dutch economy to face deep economic recession due to pandemic
snippet: The economic damage inflicted by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic is of such severity that a deep, almost globe-spanning economic recession is unavoidable...

title: Speech Klaas Knot - “On financing the energy transition”
snippet: On 8 July, Klaas Knot spoke at the Forum Analysis on financing the transition to a net-zero society. He said that the bulk of the much needed investments will have to come from the private sector, but that there is a loud and clear sine qua non.

title: Speech Nicole Stolk - The journey towards a data-driven organisation
Financial sector has €11.4 billion exposure to Russia
snippet: The latest figures available from DNB show that the Dutch financial sector had a direct exposure to Russia of approximately €11.4 billion in the fourth quarter of 2021.

title: Financial position of Dutch pension funds improved in second quarter of 2021
snippet: In the second quarter of 2021, Dutch pension funds saw their financial position improve for the fifth consecutive quarter, as growth in their aggregate pension assets outstripped the increase in liabilities.

title: Stress tests show resilience of European banking system
snippet: The European Banking Authority (EBA) and the European Central Bank (ECB) this evening published the results of the European banking stress tests carried out recently.

title: Euro banknote counterfeiting fell during COVID-19 crisis
snippet: In the first half of 2020 just over 15,700 counterfeit euro banknotes were withdrawn from circulation in the Netherlands. This was 23% less than in the first half of 2019. The decrease was most marked in the second quarter of 2020 (-47%) and can be attributed to the economic lockdown in the...

title: DNB calls for new agreements about cash
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) calls on stakeholders in the payment chain to make agreements to ensure that cash remains readily accessible and available in the Netherlands in the next five years. DNB announced this today after outgoing Minister of Finance Wopke Hoekstra had presented...

title: Five questions about the impact of the new sustainable finance strategy
snippet: DNB launches its new sustainable finance strategy. Five questions about the impact on the economy, the financial sector and consumers.

title: Working under the bonnet of our payment system
snippet: Our payment system relies heavily on non-European service providers, leaving us vulnerable. And that is why we are now seeking European solutions to address this problem. In her latest payment blog, Inge van Dijk discusses the workings of our payment system.

title: Unlocking Europe’s Financial Potential: Innovation, Regulation, and Trust
snippet: ‘We are doing what we can as central banks to facilitate adoption of new technology. It is up to you in the private sector to demonstrate where it will be used.’, said Steven Maijoor at the OPTIC event of the Association for Financial Markets in Europe (AFME), in Amsterdam.

title: Financing by Dutch fintechs more than doubled over three years
snippet: According to recent data published by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), lending via Dutch fintech platforms increased by €0.9 billion to a total of €4.4 billion in 2024, representing year-on-year growth of 27%. The majority of this financing was directed toward small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

title: Counting What’s Missing: Building Sustainability Statistics in a Data-Scarce World
snippet: ‘Good data, and good statistics based on that data, are key to making informed decisions in a complex world and a modern economy.’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the opening of the IFC Satellite Seminar on Sustainability data issues and central banks, in Amsterdam.

title: Dutch institutions suffered losses on European government bonds in first half of 2025
snippet: In the first half of 2025, the total value of Dutch institutions’ holdings in foreign government bonds declined by €23 billion, according to new figures from De Nederlandsche Bank. The losses were primarily concentrated in government bonds issued by countries in Europe, driven by interest rates.

title: Inflation differential with euro area calls for structural solutions
snippet: Inflation in the Netherlands has been higher than in the euro area as a whole for some time. Yet this inflation differential has hardly led to more balanced economic conditions.

title: Fine for Aux Cayes Fintech Co. Ltd. for offering crypto services in the Netherlands without the legally required registration from July 2023 to August 2024
snippet: On 27 May 2025, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €2,250,000 on Aux Cayes Fintech Co. Ltd. (Aux Cayes), operating under the trade name 'OKX'.

title: How inflation expectations affect households
snippet: If you think prices will rise, then there is a good chance they will. A look into the world of inflation expectations and why they play such a major role in our economy.

title: What is the impact of inflation on wages, assets and debt?
snippet: Everyone feels the effects of inflation differently. How you deal with inflation depends partly on your wages, assets and debt. We explain below.

title: Merchants see potential in an offline digital euro
snippet: Merchants in the Netherlands are showing interest in the possibilities of an 'offline' digital euro, a payment method that can still be used when there is no electricity or internet connection. However, one key condition stands out: the costs associated with using the digital euro must remain low.

title: How inflation affects households differently
snippet: How hard you are hit by inflation depends a lot on your spending patterns. But also on how much you can change your spending habits and what proportion of your income you spend on fixed expenses. Lower-income households are hit harder by inflation than groups that earn more. Why is that?

title: Fine for bunq B.V. for insufficient customer due diligence
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) on 6 May 2025 imposed an administrative fine of €2.6 million on bunq B.V. (bunq) for serious deficiencies in its anti-money laundering controls during the period under review, from January 2021 to May 2022.

title: Investing in defence companies more popular among households
snippet: Dutch households are investing more and more in defence companies, new figures from DNB show. Germany’s Rheinmetall has become particularly popular. In Q2 of 2025, it became the first defence contractor to be among the top 25 companies in which households invest directly.

title: International Working Conference: Building a Primary Product-level Emissions Data Platform
snippet: There is growing demand worldwide for accurate, comparable, and verifiable primary emissions data at the product-level.

title: Banks are lending more for residential mortgage loans
snippet: Mortgage lending by banks in the Netherlands is growing robustly again after a temporary downturn, new figures from DNB show. Growth is even above the euro area average. Loans with fixed-interest periods of five to ten years in particular are in demand.

title: Pension sector funding ratio improves in second quarter
snippet: In the second quarter of 2025, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios improve relative to the previous quarter, as the value of their liabilities decreased, while the value of their investments went up.

title: Why the ECB has kept its interest rates unchanged
snippet: For the first time in more than a year, the ECB did not lower its key interest rate but kept it unchanged at 2%. Does this mean inflation is under control? Or are there other factors at play, and is the ECB just taking a breather? A look at some of the ECB's considerations.

title: Tell us what you think: how can we make our data more relevant to you?
snippet: How much do Dutch people save? How do pension funds invest their money? And what would happen to the economy if we all went on holiday at the same time? Our statistics help answer these questions – and more. In our articles, we go beyond the numbers to explain what they mean.

title: Card payments further up, especially online
snippet: New figures from DNB show that the Dutch used their debit or credit cards to pay for €198 billion worth of products and services in 2024. This represents a 15% increase from 2022. Although point-of-sale card payments still far outnumber them, online card payments in particular are on the rise.

title: Energy inflation hits low-income households harder
snippet: Lower-income households spend a higher proportion of their income on energy. To help these households, targeted government support is more effective than generic compensation for increased costs. This was revealed in a new study conducted by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

title: Order subject to penalty for Peken Global Limited for offering crypto services in the Netherlands without the legally required registration
snippet: On 5 August 2024, DNB imposed an order subject to penalty on Peken Global Limited (PGL), operating under the trade name ‘KuCoin’. The order subject to penalty was imposed because PGL provided crypto services in the Netherlands without registration with DNB, which is against the law.

title: Klaas Knot: 14 years in 14 figures (and 5 videos)
snippet: Two times seven years. This is the maximum. And that is why Klaas Knot is now handing over the presidential baton to his successor, Olaf Sleijpen. Olaf will be leading a central bank that has changed considerably since Klaas started – just like the world around it.

title: Current account balance remains high
snippet: In the first quarter, the current account balance was 9,9% of GDP, almost the same as last year. Despite rising geopolitical tensions, imports and exports of goods and services increased.

title: The Dutch support cash regardless of whether they use it
snippet: Dutch people are still strongly attached to cash as a payment option. This is according to a survey commissioned by De Nederlandsche Bank. An overwhelming majority of respondents (92%) say that being able to pay with cash is socially important.

title: Central counterparties: central to protecting financial stability
snippet: ‘CCP’s are almost by nature global institutions that thrive on global cooperation and multilateralism. The more the industry can do by itself in order to improve the robustness and transparency of its activities, the better’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the annual meeting of central counterparties

title: Instruction issued to trust offices ABiLiTieS Trust B.V. and The Netherlands Trust Services B.V. for shortcomings in their SIRA and customer due diligence
snippet: On 14 May 2024, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) issued an instruction to trust offices ABiLiTieS Trust B.V. and The Netherlands Trust Services B.V. (Abilities and NTS) for shortcomings found in their systematic integrity risk analysis (SIRA) and the customer due diligence.

title: Fine for ABN AMRO Bank N.V. for non-compliance with bonus ban
snippet: On 10 June 2025, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed a €15 million fine on ABN AMRO Bank N.V. (ABN AMRO) for non-compliance with the bonus ban.

title: Dutch public are positive about the euro
snippet: The Dutch remain confident in the euro, even in times of economic uncertainty. This is according to a recently published survey by Eurobarometer, the European Commission’s survey instrument. It also shows that support for the single currency in the euro area is at its highest level on record.

title: Financial stability: it's not glamorous, but it matters
snippet: ‘Financial stability affects households, businesses, governments—and ultimately, the trust that underpins our economies’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the opening of the 9th Macroprudential Conference, at DNB in Amsterdam today.

title: Weaker US dollar hits pension funds harder than falling stock prices
snippet: In the first quarter of 2025, the total value of Dutch pension funds' investments went down €54 billion (-3%), new figures from DNB show. In foreign investments, negative exchange rate movements in particular contributed to the losses

title: Olaf Sleijpen new President of De Nederlandsche Bank
snippet: Olaf Sleijpen will become the new president of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) from 1 July 2025. On the recommendation of DNB’s Supervisory Board, Minister of Finance Eelco Heinen on Friday nominated Olaf Sleijpen for appointment by Royal Decree.

title: Innovation we can trust: the role of DNB in regulating FinTechs
snippet: ‘A license from a respected regulator helps your business build trust with customers, investors, and partners.’, said Gita Salden at the conference ‘FinTech meets the regulators’ at DNB, Amsterdam, today.

title: How is the water? Continuing our work to preserve financial stability
snippet: ‘Financial stability affects households, businesses, governments—and ultimately, the trust that underpins our economies.’, said Klaas Knot at a Financial Stability conference at Banco de España today.

title: Instruction issued to trust office DTS Dutch Trust Services B.V. for shortcomings identified in its SIRA and customer due diligence
snippet: On 14 May 2024, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) issued an instruction to trust office DTS Dutch Trust Services B.V. (DTS) for shortcomings found in its systematic integrity risk analysis (SIRA) and customer due diligence. At DTS’s request

title: Instruction for Erez Corporate Service B.V. for various shortcomings in performing its gatekeeper role
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) issued an instruction to Erez Corporate Service B.V. (Erez) on 3 June 2021

title: Remarks for the 93rd G30 Plenary in Berlin – 7 June 2025
snippet: ‘A fundamental principle that guides the FSB’s work is that we do not pick winners. Our focus is on ensuring that innovation develops safely and responsibly, within the boundaries of our public policy objectives.’, said Klaas Knot today at the G30 plenary meeting in Berlin.

title: Uncertainty and trade tensions weigh on economic growth
snippet: The Dutch economy is set to grow by 1.1% in 2025. Uncertainty and trade tensions will continue to mute economic growth at around 1% a year for the following two years. This is according to the Spring Projections as published by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) on Friday.

title: Development impact fees – what difference could they make?
snippet: The Dutch housing market is tight, making houses difficult to afford. While more houses are needed, high land prices and other obstacles are hindering new construction.

title: Off the beaten path: what we learned during the renovation at Frederiksplein
snippet: ‘ The importance of the BREEAM and WELL certificates reaches further than just this building. It shows that sustainable construction in the Netherlands is feasible, affordable and formidable.’, said Klaas Knot in Amsterdam today.

title: Suri-Change’ licences withdrawn for failure to meet statutory obligations
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) on 18 October 2023 decided to withdraw the licences of B.V. Suri-Change (SC), a money exchange and payment institution with offices in Rotterdam, The Hague and Amsterdam.

title: Banking on buffers: why we need resilience in times of uncertainty
snippet: ‘There is no trade-off between financial stability and economic growth. Rather, financial stability is a necessary precondition for sustainable economic growth.’, said Klaas Knot in his opening address for the SSM Round Table, in Amsterdam today.

title: Dutch corporate bank lending picks up
snippet: Recent years have seen Dutch banks lend more to domestic businesses, following a period in which growth in corporate lending lagged behind the euro area average. This is according to new figures from DNB which are discussed in the Dutch economists’ journal ESB today.

title: Talent is worth its weight in gold
snippet: ‘The complex challenges we face every day - climate risks, the digital transformation, and geopolitical tensions - demand a rainbow of opinions, insights, and perspectives.’, said Klaas Knot during the ‘Talent to the Top’ event at DNB in Amsterdam today. He spoke there about DNB’s diversity policy.

title: Tough love: the importance of the internal audit function for central banks
snippet: ‘If we do not live up to the standards we impose on others, we lose all authority.’, said Olaf Sleijpen at an international conference of central bank internal auditors at DNB, Amsterdam. He spoke about the importance of internal auditing for central banks and what it takes to be a good auditor.

title: Broader definition of income leads to lower current account surplus
snippet: Based on a broader definition of investment income, the average Dutch current account surplus for the period 2021-2023 falls from 8.8% to 7.5%. This has emerged from an analysis conducted by DNB. The broader definition is in line with a recent International Monetary Fund (IMF) recommendation.

title: Value of Dutch households' investments falls slightly in first quarter of 2025, relatively high losses in tech stocks
snippet: In the first quarter of 2025, the value of Dutch households’ portfolio investments fell slightly, as revealed by the latest DNB figures. At the end of March, the value of investments stood at €188.9 billion, compared to €189.7 billion in the previous quarter (-0.4%, revised figures).

title: NFPS advice: Prepare for a three-day disruption of electronic payments
snippet: Consumers and retailers should be prepared for emergency situations in which the payment system is down for 72 hours. That could be the case if payment terminals are not working, ATMs are down or online banking cannot be used.

title: Global economic uncertainty leads to higher financial stability risks
snippet: The outlook for financial stability in the Netherlands has deteriorated due to geopolitical tensions and high economic uncertainty. In particular, uncertainty around trade, international cooperation and government budgets has risen sharply in recent months.

title: Instruction for IQ EQ Netherlands N.V. for insufficient customer due diligence
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) issued an instruction to IQ EQ Netherlands N.V. (IQ EQ) on 5 March 2024 following an investigation in 2023, for failing to carry out sufficient customer due diligence.

title: A true treasure: why we need diversity and inclusion in the financial industry
snippet: ‘We have to ensure that human uniqueness is not just tolerated, but treasured in our financial institutions.’, said Klaas Knot today at the International Diversity and Inclusion Conference at DNB, Amsterdam.

title: A race we cannot afford to lose: cybersecurity in an age of geopolitical tensions
snippet: ‘To keep financial institutions and the financial system safe, resilience against cyberattacks has become just as important as holding sufficient capital and liquidity.’, said Steven Maijoor at the ISDA Annual General Meeting in Amsterdam today.

title: Cash acceptance in the Netherlands slightly down
snippet: The number of ‘PIN only’ points of sale has increased slightly from 4.5% in 2023 to 4.8% in 2024. The increase is most noticeable in the larger cities, and particularly at pharmacies and cinemas.

title: How uncertainty can slow down the Dutch economy
snippet: Trade conflicts and geopolitical tensions are resulting in historically high economic uncertainty worldwide. While much of the uncertainty originates abroad, its implications are also felt here in the Netherlands.

title: Productivity growth remains remarkably stable in much of the Dutch business sector
snippet: In contrast to the general labour productivity growth trend in the Dutch economy, which has exhibited a marked deceleration, labour productivity growth in the market sector has demonstrated notable stability over the course of several years.

title: How the US tariffs can harm the Dutch economy
snippet: On 2 April, President Trump’s announcement of "reciprocal tariffs" sent a shockwave through the global trading system and financial markets. If these exceptionally high tariffs are actually implemented, they would affect the Dutch economy mainly through a decline in global trade.

title: Pension sector funding ratio improves in first quarter
snippet: In the first quarter of 2025, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios improve relative to the previous quarter, as the value of their liabilities decreased more than the value of their investments. Total investments decreased by 5.8% to €1,589 billion...

title: Agnostic or preaching the gospel: what the state of the world implies for ECB monetary policy and the role of the euro
snippet: ‘A more widespread use of the euro would be a good thing for Europeans.’, said Klaas Knot in his speech at the Peterson Institute in Washington today. He spoke about what the current economic situation means for the ECB’s monetary policy and for the international use of the euro.

title: Majority of Dutch people willing to use digital euro
snippet: Unknown does not necessarily mean unloved. DNB research shows that a majority of Dutch people would consider using the digital euro, should this digital counterpart to cash become available in the future.

title: Stating the obvious: a central bankers perspective on resilience in times of uncertainty
snippet: ‘Multilateralism is enlightened self-interest. It’s transactional, but in a smart way. It’s not always the easiest way, but in the long term it is the best way. That is the lesson we learned in post-war Europe.’, said Klaas Knot in his speech at Eurofi in Warsaw today.

title: Conference on Globalisation and geo-economic fragmentation: follow via livestream on 9 April
snippet: On 9 April 2025 together with Bruegel we are organising a conference on Globalisation and geo-economic fragmentation.

title: Significant growth in securitisations in 2024 after years of contraction
snippet: After almost two decades of contraction, outstanding Dutch securitisations sold to investors increased substantially in 2024, new figures from DNB show. Net growth was €3.1 billion (12%) to €29.2 billion, still considerably less than 20 years ago.

title: Standing our ground: auditors and supervisors in the world of geopolitics
snippet: ‘When politicians start to drift, independent experts, like in the IAASB, IASB and the Basel Committee, must stand firm. We need to continue explaining the advantages for countries to play by the rules, even if others don’t.

title: DNB studies industry resilience to cost increases
snippet: From zinc smelters to asphalt producers, and from food producers to refineries – energy and emissions costs are determining factors for the output of much of Dutch industry.

title: Fine for trust office Amicorp for insufficient customer due diligence
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €530.450,- on trust office Amicorp Netherlands B.V. (Amicorp) on 25 March 2025. The fine was imposed because the customer due diligence carried out by Amicorp did not meet the legal requirements.

title: Younger and older people in particular are more likely to pay by debit transaction
snippet: The share of debit transactions in total payments at the checkout remained unchanged at 80% in 2024, but there are notable outliers among certain age groups.

title: Ban on value transfer for pension fund Trespa due to a disproportionate balance of interests
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) on 30 July 2024 prohibited a proposed collective value transfer of Stichting Pensioenfonds Trespa in liquidation (Trespa). In this news release, we explain how we came to this decision.

title: ‘European cooperation essential to confront geopolitical risks’
snippet: Today, De Nederlandsche Bank publishes ‘Resilience in turbulent times’, a study on the potential impact of geopolitical risks on financial institutions. DNB economist Maurice Doll co-wrote the study and talks about its main findings.

title: United States largest international investor in the Netherlands
snippet: The United States has been the largest net international investor in the Netherlands for years, balance of payments figures from DNB show. This is due to investments by US multinationals in Dutch subsidiaries. Much of these investments flow out of the Netherlands to business units in other countries

title: Robust policies in an uncertain world
snippet: We are facing geopolitical instability with the threat of a global trade war on top of a war in Ukraine that has been raging for three years. The world has been turned upside down again in recent weeks. Understandably, this has led to high levels of anxiety and uncertainty among citizens.

title: Introductory remarks upon the presentation of the 2024 annual report
snippet: ‘We in the Netherlands have little influence on many of the developments currently taking place in the world. But we can do one thing. And that is to work to mitigate the economic consequences and perhaps seize new opportunities.’ Klaas Knot said this at the presentation of DNB’s 2024 Annual Report.

title: Dutch portfolio investments total nearly €3,500 billion
snippet: Dutch firms, institutions and households collectively held nearly €3,500 billion worth of securities as at year-end 2024. This is according to new figures DNB today released for the first time. From now on, DNB charts the securities holdings of the overall Dutch economy.

title: The impact of government policies on inflation
snippet: While inflation in the euro area is heading towards the 2% target over the course of this year, inflation in the Netherlands remains persistently higher than expected. In our new analysis, we show that the impact on inflation varies for each policy measure and depends on the state of the economy.

title: Dutch pension funds invest more in US companies than in European companies
snippet: Dutch pension funds invest structurally less in European companies than in US companies, DNB figures reveal. At the end of 2024, invested assets in European (EU) non-financial corporations amounted to €97 billion, compared to €293 billion in US counterparts.

title: De Nieuwe Schatkamer is open
snippet: De Nieuwe Schatkamer is located on three floors of the Amsterdam headquarters of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB). Anyone interested in learning about gold, money or the economy is welcome.

title: DNB headquarters officially opened by King Willem-Alexander on 26 March
snippet: On 26 March, His Majesty King Willem-Alexander will perform the official opening ceremony together with the President of De Nederlandsche Bank, Klaas Knot, in the presence of some 350 invited guests.

title: Chris Figee appointed to DNB Supervisory Board from 1 March
snippet: Chris Figee will join the Supervisory Board of De Nederlandsche Bank from 1 March. Figee has been appointed by Finance minister Eelco Heinen on behalf of the shareholder on the nomination of DNB’s Supervisory Board, for an initial four-year term.

title: Royal honour for Paul Hilbers
snippet: King Willem-Alexander has appointed Professor Paul Hilbers as Commander of the Order of Orange-Nassau for his services to society. On Friday, 14 February, the Dutch Minister of Finance Eelco Heinen appointed him with the royal decoration.

title: Households with investments close 2024 with record securities holdings
snippet: In the fourth quarter of 2024, Dutch households’ portfolio investments reached a new record high of €192.4 billion, as revealed by the latest DNB figures. The increase is entirely due to rising stock market prices, as households also sold a significant amount of their securities holdings.

title: The case for international monetary diplomacy
snippet: ‘What we need now is for governments, central banks and academia to continue to speak out for the international financial rules-based order that has brought us stability and prosperity over the decades.’, said Klaas Knot at Nyenrode Business University today.

title: Dealing with geo-economic fragmentation
snippet: ‘Our task as central bankers is to try to limit the economic cost of the current global political climate. […] By pointing to the economic and social costs of protectionist policies.

title: Cross-border implications of the modernization of payment systems
snippet: ‘The modernization of payment systems has cross-border implications and presents both significant opportunities and notable risks. As we embrace these innovations, we must remain vigilant and proactive in managing the associated risks to ensure the stability and resilience of our financial systems.’

title: Cyber resilience in an age of geopolitical tensions
snippet: What if a large scale state-sponsored cyberattack is launched on the financial sector of an EU member state? How much damage would it cause? How long would it take to recover? In his speech at the Annual FinTech and Regulation Conference in Brussels today, Steven Maijoor addressed these questions.

title: From Frankfurt with love: 14 years on the ECB’s Governing Council
snippet: In the first Klaas Knot Lecture on international economic policy, initiated by the University of Groningen, Klaas Knot said ‘we should aim to design our policy choices in such a way that they are robust across different outcomes, rather than focusing on only one scenario’.

title: Fine for de Volksbank N.V. for deficient anti-money laundering controls
snippet: On 22 January 2025, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €5 million on de Volksbank N.V. (de Volksbank) for serious shortcomings in its anti-money laundering controls.

title: Administrative fine for de Volksbank N.V. for failure to ensure sound business operations
snippet: On 22 January 2025, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €15 million on de Volksbank N.V. (de Volksbank). The fine was imposed because, at least during the period under review, between 2018 and 2023...

title: Fines totalling €20 million imposed on de Volksbank
snippet: On 22 January 2025, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed two administrative fines on de Volksbank. One amounts to €15 million for failing to ensure the sound conduct of business operations. The other, of €5 million, was imposed for deficient anti-money laundering controls.

title: Dutch households keep saving: more than €600 billion in bank accounts
snippet: Dutch households again saved a lot of money in 2024, new figures from DNB show. Together, they held a record amount of €600.5 billion in payment and savings accounts at the end of December 2024.

title: Average funding ratio of Dutch pension sector declined
snippet: In the fourth quarter of 2024, Dutch pension funds saw their funding ratios decline relative to the third quarter, as the value of their liabilities increased more than the value of their investments.

title: ECB has stopped reinvestments in maturing bonds
snippet: From October 2014 to mid-2022, the Eurosystem purchased government and corporate bonds to boost inflation. Also known among economists as Quantitative Easing (QE), the asset purchase programme was set up when policy rates could not be lowered further.

title: Relative price of services recovers after pandemic
snippet: The prices of services in the Netherlands are rising faster than the prices of goods. This trend was temporarily broken during the COVID pandemic due to supply chain issues, as revealed by new DNB figures.

title: Cash remains a key payment method in Europe, but its share continues to decline
snippet: Digital payments are on the rise in the euro area, but cash was still the payment instrument used most often at points of sale (POS) in 2024. More than half (52%) of all POS transactions were paid in cash in 2024.

title: DNB and ATI end cooperation on Bonaire
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) and Across The Isles (ATI) have decided to end their cooperation on the 'Across the Seas' project on Bonaire, following extensive mutual consultations in recent weeks.

title: DNB returns to renewed and open headoffice
snippet: Employees of De Nederlandsche Bank will return to the headquarters building on Frederiksplein in Amsterdam on 6 January 2025. Nearly five years of renovation work have resulted in a building that is ready for the future, sustainable and open for all.

title: Import surplus in goods trade with US shrinks
snippet: The negative balance in the goods trade with the United States has weakened in recent quarters after rising sharply since 2021, as revealed by new DNB balance of payments figures. In the third quarter of 2024, the balance was € -3.7 billion.

title: Financing through fintechs nearly doubled
snippet: The volume of financing provided through fintech platforms operated by non-bank parties has almost doubled in two years, according to new global research by DNB and the Financial Stability Board (FSB). In the Netherlands, this type of lending amounted to €2.3 billion by the end of 2023.

title: Geopolitical shocks have a significant impact on the solvency of Dutch and European insurers
snippet: Geopolitical shocks have a significant impact on the solvency of Dutch and European insurers. This has emerged from a stress test published by the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) on 17 December 2024.

title: Economic growth continues, uncertainty increases
snippet: In the Netherlands, economic growth is set to accelerate in the coming years, but geopolitical uncertainty is increasingly threatening the Dutch economy. In addition, at 3%, inflation in the Netherlands will remain higher than in the euro area in the years ahead.

title: Income flowing to tax havens through the Netherlands structurally down
snippet: Income from foreign direct investment in the Netherlands flowing to low-tax jurisdictions has declined structurally since 2020, new figures from DNB show. Income flows with other countries remained more stable over the same period.

title: Investor interest in Dutch mortgage funds continues to decline
snippet: Dutch mortgage funds received €2 billion in new investments from institutional investors such as pension funds and insurers in the first three quarters of 2024, DNB figures show. This is less than in previous years and can be attributed to market interest rates having risen sharply during 2022.

title: On Phronesis and Price Stability
snippet: ‘With phronesis – practical wisdom. That is how the Eurosystem operates,’ said Klaas Knot on 28 November, at the Euro50 Group’s 25th anniversary. He illustrated this with three examples: the ECB's balance sheet policy, the change in the neutral interest rate (r*) and recent supply shocks.

title: DNB issues instruction to Stichting Pensioenfonds PostNL for transferring assets to employer in violation of statutory conditions
snippet: On 21 December 2023, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) issued an instruction to Stichting Pensioenfonds PostNL because the pension fund had agreed to reduce a claim of around €80 million on the employer, PostNL N.V., to around €60 million.

title: Klaas Knot at Room for Discussion (studentsUvA)
snippet: On 7 November, Klaas Knot was a guest at Room for Discussion, the interview programme of students from the University of Amsterdam. How does Knot experience the challenges in the field of monetary policy? How do you balance economic growth, financial stability and the fight against inflation?

title: When economists agree: the role of central banks in the green transition
snippet: ‘The long-term cost of dealing with the consequences of climate change, if we do nothing or too little, far outweighs the short-term cost of an orderly and timely transition.’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the Green Finance Symposium at Tilburg University.

title: Geopolitics and Economics: a high-traffic intersection
snippet: ‘Geopolitical tensions can slow down economic growth, increase trade costs, and, most important for central bankers, lead to higher inflation,’ said Klaas Knot at DNB’s Annual Research Conference in Amsterdam, on 21 November 2024.

title: From ding dong to bleep bleep: promoting innovative retail payments markets in a fragmented world
snippet: ‘Strategic autonomy in retail payments means there also needs to be a European option, where Europe can independently manage its payments ecosystem.’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the annual conference of the European Payment Institutions Federation (EPIF) in Brussels today.

title: Household portfolio investments reach another all-time high in third quarter of 2024
snippet: In the third quarter of 2024, portfolio investments of Dutch households reached a new record level of €190.4 billion, new figures from DNB show. This is around 2% up from the previous all-time high recorded in the preceding quarter.

title: Risks to financial stability in autumn 2024
snippet: ‘Given the growing cyber risks, we must continue our work to reduce the probability of cyberattacks while simultaneously boosting our resilience against their potential impact.’, said Olaf Sleijpen at the IIF International Accounting and Reporting Forum.

title: Growing geopolitical risks impact financial sector
snippet: The heightened international tensions can have an impact on financial institutions, according to De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) in its supervisory strategy for 2025-2028 and in a study on the impact of geopolitical risks on financial institutions.

title: Beyond the rules: promoting an ethical culture in central banks and supervisory authorities
snippet: ‘If we are to live up to the high standards we set for ourselves, we need rules, but first and foremost we need an ethical culture.’ said Klaas Knot in his speech at the DNB Ethics and Compliance Conference. He spoke about promoting an ethical culture in central banks and supervisory authorities.

title: Fine for Bybit Fintech Limited for offering crypto services in the Netherlands without the legally required registration until September 2023
snippet: On 22 October 2024, De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of €2,250,000 on Bybit Fintech Limited (Bybit). The fine was imposed because Bybit provided crypto services in the Netherlands without the legally required registration with DNB, which is against the law.

title: Partly cloudy skies in the euro area, with a silver lining
snippet: ‘While macro indicators point to a soft landing, we do not foresee a recession in the euro area. Also, the financial sector is resilient and inflation is getting close to target.’, said Klaas Knot at the G30 International Banking Seminar.

title: Strengthening Financial Resilience: Lessons from Pittsburgh
snippet: Speaking at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum held in New York on 22 October 2024, Klaas Knot looked back at the 2009 G20 in Pittsburgh and the measures taken since then to combat the financial crisis and strengthen the global financial system.

title: Financial stability in balance, risks remain
snippet: Financial stability in the Netherlands has been buoyed in recent months by an improving economy and upbeat sentiment in financial markets, following a brief period of turbulence in the summer. Steadily falling inflation in the euro area and a ‘soft landing’ of the economy contribute to stability.

title: Want a strong financial system? Implement Basel III
snippet: ‘The opposition to Basel III reflects a kind of short-term thinking, that, frankly, I find hard to understand.’, said Klaas Knot today in speech before the IIEB, an group of European bankers.

title: Lean and clean: Europe’s coordinated fight against money laundering
snippet: ‘Trust in the financial system and in our rule of law will never be for sale. Crime should not pay. Not in any way. Ever,’ concluded Gita Salden at the international workshop on the European anti-money laundering framework, organised by DNB on 10 October 2024.

title: Carbon footprint of Dutch insurers and pension funds in sharper focus
snippet: Dutch insurers and pension funds invest not only directly in listed equity and corporate bonds, but also indirectly via investment funds. New DNB figures on CO2 emissions of non-financial corporations relate to both types of investments and provide a more complete..

title: 2024: An AI odyssey
snippet: ‘We encourage the use of AI to its full potential, while respecting the rules and regulations that ensure the stability and integrity of the financial system and that uphold our values of fairness, freedom and security,’ said Steven Maijoor at the kick-off event of the impact centre ‘AI4 Fintech’.

title: Mirjam van Praag reappointed to DNB’s Supervisory Board
snippet: Prof. Mirjam van Praag has been reappointed to the Supervisory Board of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) effective from 1 October 2024. Minister of Finance Eelco Heinen, representing the Shareholder, decided this on the recommendation of the Supervisory Board.

title: DNB develops new model to forecast short-term economic growth
snippet: Based on a new forecast model, DNB expects the Dutch economy to grow by 0.4% in the third quarter of 2024 compared to the previous quarter. The uncertainty surrounding this forecast is large. In mid-November, CBS publishes the first official measurement of economic growth in the third quarter.

title: Instruction issued to Amicorp Netherlands B.V. for insufficient customer due diligence and for not having an effective compliance function
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) issued an instruction to Amicorp Netherlands B.V. (Amicorp) on 31 May 2024 for Amicorp's insufficient customer due diligence and lack of an effective compliance function.

title: Esther Bunnik neuw Head of the Communications department
snippet: Esther Bunnik has been appointed Head of the Communications department with effect from 15 November 2024. She succeeds Ben Feiertag, who is leaving DNB from 1 December.

title: Dutch current account balance remained almost unchanged despite larger export surplus
snippet: The current account surplus of the Netherlands’ balance of payments was €24.8 billion in the second quarter of 2024, almost the same as the corresponding period last year, new figures from DNB show.

title: Under new European budget rules it is important to remain well below the 3% deficit limit
snippet: New European fiscal rules entered into force in April. Although more realistic, they are far-reaching, especially for high-debt countries. Whether they prompt Member States to reduce over-indebtedness will depend on compliance and enforcement.

title: Opening Vissering exhibition Ankara
snippet: ‘Inflation in Türkiye has come down significantly. I think this is an accomplishment that should not be underestimated.’, said Klaas Knot in his short speech at the Turkish central bank.

title: The mission of Gerard Vissering: why we need independent central banks
snippet: ‘Monetary policy credibility does not come overnight. It has to be earned. Again and again.’ , said Klaas Knot in his speech at Koç University, Istanbul. He spoke about the need for independent central banks to face the challenges of our times.

title: Painting like Rembrandt: managing risks in the age of AI
snippet: ‘Many of the potential risks of AI may seem new, but if you look beneath the surface, they are strikingly similar to traditional financial risks. Risks that we are familiar with’, said Steven Maijoor at a Bloomberg event in Amsterdam on September 16th.

title: A look at post-retirement income
snippet: By and large, households in the Netherlands are able to replace approximately 60% of their previous income with a state pension (AOW) and supplementary retirement income, and 63% if savings are included.

title: On flood management and financial stability
